items.q: Shock is most accurately defined as which state?
o: Systolic pressure below a fixed cutoff
Systemic hypoperfusion with inadequate tissue oxygenation
Low cardiac output in every case
items.exp: Shock is systemic hypoperfusion causing cellular hypoxia, whatever the blood pressure. Distributive shock may even have high output, so low output does not define all shock.
r: Incorrect. Pressure cutoffs miss compensated shock.
Correct. Shock means hypoperfusion and tissue hypoxia.
Incorrect. Tachycardia and fever are non-specific signs.
Incorrect. Septic shock may have high cardiac output.
items.kp: Define shock by perfusion, not by pressure alone.

items.q: Cardiac tamponade causing shock belongs to which mechanistic class?
items.exp: Tamponade obstructs cardiac filling from outside the heart, so it is obstructive shock. Relief requires pericardial drainage, not simply fluids or inotropes.
r: Incorrect. Distributive shock is vasodilatory, as in sepsis.
Correct. Tamponade obstructs filling: obstructive shock.
Incorrect. Circulating volume is not primarily lost.
Incorrect. The muscle itself is not the primary failure.
items.kp: Tamponade and massive PE are obstructive shock.

items.q: Early septic shock most often shows which peripheral finding?
items.exp: Early septic shock is distributive with vasodilation, so peripheries often feel warm despite tissue hypoperfusion and rising lactate. Later stages may become cold as output falls.
r: Incorrect. Cold limbs typify hypovolaemic or cardiogenic shock.
Correct. Warm peripheries typify early distributive shock.
Incorrect. Pupil signs do not classify shock.
Incorrect. Bowel sounds do not define the shock type.
items.kp: Warm shock still shocks: check lactate and mentation.

items.q: Which laboratory marker best reflects anaerobic metabolism in shock?
items.exp: Lactate accumulates when hypoperfused cells rely on anaerobic glycolysis, so serial lactate tracks severity and response. It is not specific to one shock type.
r: Incorrect. Albumin does not track acute perfusion.
Correct. Lactate reflects anaerobic metabolism in shock.
Incorrect. Urea changes have many causes.
Incorrect. Platelets do not measure tissue oxygenation.
items.kp: Follow lactate trends in any shock type.

items.q: The nonprogressive stage of shock is maintained mainly by which response?
items.exp: Compensated shock uses baroreceptor reflexes, sympathetic tachycardia and vasoconstriction to protect heart and brain. Lysosomal release marks irreversible injury instead.
r: Incorrect. Lysosomal release signals irreversible damage.
Correct. Sympathetic compensation defines the early stage.
Incorrect. Coagulation activation is a complication, not compensation.
Incorrect. Leak worsens rather than compensates shock.
items.kp: Compensation means reflex vasoconstriction and tachycardia.

items.q: Prolonged shock most characteristically injures the kidney by which lesion?
items.exp: Sustained renal hypoperfusion causes acute tubular necrosis with muddy brown casts and rising creatinine. Glomerular diseases have immune mechanisms unrelated to shock perfusion.
r: Incorrect. Crescents reflect severe glomerular inflammation.
Correct. Shock causes ischaemic acute tubular necrosis.
Incorrect. Membranous disease is an immune glomerular lesion.
Incorrect. Cystic change is genetic, not shock related.
items.kp: Shock kidney means acute tubular necrosis.

items.q: Neurogenic shock after spinal cord injury combines hypotension with which unusual sign?
items.exp: Loss of sympathetic tone causes vasodilation with warm skin and unopposed vagal bradycardia. This contrasts with most shock states where tachycardia compensates.
r: Incorrect. Fever and tachycardia suggest sepsis.
Correct. Bradycardia with warm skin signals neurogenic shock.
Incorrect. Bronchospasm and urticaria signal anaphylaxis.
Incorrect. Pulsus paradoxus signals tamponade physiology.
items.kp: Hypotension plus bradycardia after cord injury means neurogenic shock.

items.q: Anaphylactic shock is primarily which mechanistic type?
items.exp: Anaphylaxis causes mediator driven vasodilation and capillary leak, a distributive shock. Adrenaline is the immediate life saving treatment because it reverses vasodilation and bronchospasm.
r: Incorrect. Obstruction here is airway swelling, but shock class is distributive.
Correct. Anaphylaxis is distributive shock.
Incorrect. Volume is maldistributed and leaked, not bled.
Incorrect. Pump failure is not the primary defect.
items.kp: Anaphylaxis equals distributive shock; adrenaline first.

items.q: Bilateral adrenal haemorrhage in fulminant meningococcal sepsis is called what?
items.exp: Waterhouse Friderichsen syndrome is adrenal haemorrhage during overwhelming sepsis, classically meningococcal, causing acute adrenal failure within shock. It accompanies purpura and disseminated coagulation.
r: Incorrect. Addison disease is chronic adrenal insufficiency.
Correct. Sepsis related adrenal haemorrhage bears this name.
Incorrect. Cushing syndrome is cortisol excess.
Incorrect. Conn syndrome is aldosterone excess.
items.kp: Meningococcal collapse plus adrenal haemorrhage: Waterhouse Friderichsen.

items.q: Irreversible shock is distinguished by which cellular event?
o: Lysosomal enzyme release and membrane failure
items.exp: Irreversible shock involves widespread membrane damage and lysosomal enzyme release so tissues cannot recover even if pressure returns. Earlier stages remain potentially reversible.
r: Incorrect. Compensation marks the reversible early stage.
Correct. Membrane failure and lysosomal release mark irreversibility.
Incorrect. A recovering lactate suggests reversible shock.
Incorrect. Vasodilation alone does not define irreversibility.
items.kp: Once membranes fail, restoring pressure cannot save tissue.
